title: Confidential signal commons turn weak, identity-sensitive warnings into shared safety knowledge
summary: This pattern candidate names the institutional design in which weak signals, near-misses, human-factors concerns, or worker safety concerns are made reportable by confidentiality, de-identification, third-party independence, analyst triage, and public/action-facing outputs. Rev0007 promotes the pattern because the cube now has multiple source-infrastructure records; it explicitly does not claim that these systems are complete or always effective.

status_history.note: Seed identified near-miss reporting as a distinct subcorpus and ASRS-like systems as underused source infrastructure.
Promoted using ASRS, CHIRP, CIRAS, ATSB/REPCON, and NTSB recommendation-tracking infrastructure records.

time.case_range: contemporary institutional source infrastructure; source pages accessed 2026-05-24

place.scope: cross-jurisdictional: United States, United Kingdom, Republic of Ireland, Australia

claims.claim: ASRS, CHIRP, CIRAS, and REPCON support a shared source-infrastructure pattern: confidential or independent channels can protect reporters, de-identify sensitive safety concerns, and route weak signals toward organisations or authorities positioned to act.
what_would_change_status: Outcome studies or failure cases show these infrastructures lack the claimed shared structure, or require narrower subfamilies.

evidence_migration.note: rev0016 removes overloaded source_support.source_id/record_id keys and uses typed evidence_refs with ref_kind and support_role.

claims.claim: The signal-commons pattern is distinct from accident investigation: it is designed to capture pre-catastrophe, weak, human-factors, near-miss, or concern-level information; NTSB recommendation tracking provides a complementary action-memory layer after investigation.
what_would_change_status: A better taxonomy shows confidential-reporting and recommendation-tracking should not be adjacent in one pattern surface.

evidence_profile.source_depth: official/institutional source pages only; no outcome or database sampling
limitations: NTSB recommendation tracking is action-memory rather than confidential reporting and may need separate pattern later.
evidence_profile.red_team_state: rev0016 scaffold added; controls not yet promoted

type_payload.candidate_mechanism: A system increases the chance that safety-relevant information becomes institutional knowledge by protecting reporters, de-identifying sensitive reports, separating safety learning from punishment where possible, using expert/analyst triage, and routing information to organizations or authorities positioned to act.
design_primitives: limited immunity or no-blame posture when applicable
alert, report, database, newsletter, recommendation, or closure-tracking outputs
not_this: not proof that voluntary reporting is complete
not proof that confidentiality always holds
not an instruction to replace mandatory reporting
not a claim that confidential reporting alone prevents disasters
negative_controls_needed: reporting systems with low trust or low use
cases where reports were made but no action followed
mandatory-report systems with stronger outcomes than confidential voluntary systems
type_payload.query_value: Gives the cube a way to find and compare the institutions that preserve the missing denominator before disaster: near-misses, unease, operational workarounds, fatigue concerns, equipment concerns, and weak warnings.

positive_controls_needed: Add additional confidential or de-identified reporting infrastructures from safety-critical domains.
negative_controls_needed: Add open/non-confidential reporting systems and failed confidential channels to distinguish confidentiality from trust, analysis, and action routing.
counterexamples_to_seek: A channel with confidentiality but no meaningful action-memory or feedback loop.
rollback_triggers: A second-review extraction demotes or materially weakens one of the support records.
A negative-control record shows the pattern label fits too many unrelated cases.
A counterexample shows the claimed recurrence is better explained by a narrower or different mechanism.
The pattern is upgraded only after controls and not by record count alone.
red_team_controls.split_or_merge_watch: Medium: signal capture, identity protection, analyst triage, alerting, and recommendation tracking may need separate infrastructure factors.

maturity_gate.minimum_before_mature: At least one positive control, at least one negative control, an explicit counterexample search, and a rollback/split decision recorded in the claim-status ledger.

handling_notes: Pattern examples involve confidential reporting; never use the archive to pierce confidentiality or blame named reporters.
Keep reporting infrastructure separate from proof of prevention, because overclaiming safety systems repeats the corpus’s target error.
When importing de-identified reports later, preserve original sanitization and avoid combinatorial re-identification.

unknowns: Which infrastructures have measurable action closure?
How much underreporting remains despite confidentiality?
How do reporting channels interact with mandatory systems, regulators, unions, operators, and courts?
What are the failure modes of confidential reporting itself?
next_actions: Add a report-to-action exemplar for ASRS/REPCON/CIRAS/CHIRP if source-permissible.
Add negative-control cases where reporting did not produce action or where reporter trust failed.
Create a database sampling ethics protocol before importing report narratives.
Add medical/patient-safety and nuclear operating-experience analogues.
Add at least one negative-control or counterexample record before upgrading this pattern beyond candidate level.
